newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil high court backs civil service pay hike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil high court backs civil service pay hike.

text.p: Brazil's highest court on Wednesday voted in favor of a 28.9 percent pay rise for 11 civil servants, an official said.

Saying that he considered equal treatment of civil servants sacrosanct, Supreme Federal Tribunal President Sepulveda Pertence cast the final vote to make it 6-4 in favor of granting the plantiffs the same pay rise awarded to the armed forces in 1993.

The government fears that a favorable ruling, which only applies to the 11 workers, could set a precedent for the entire federal workforce and cost Brasilia billions of dollars in extra payroll expenses.
The civil service workers cited a rule that entitles public sector workers to the same pay rises awarded to state employees in other job categories.
"I am delighted," said Geraldo Magela, a lawyer for the civil servants.

Magela said that from the workers' point of view, the ruling only effects the 11 people who brought the case. But he noted that up to one million past and present state workers could theoretically bring cases against the government.
Government officials estimate that if the pay rise were extended to all federal workers, it would cost an additional $7 billion, money it says it doesn't have.
The federal government spent a total of $42 billion in payroll costs in 1996.
Proposed constitutional amendments, aimed at slashing payroll costs by allowing the government to fire workers and set pay limits, are seen as essential to slash Brazil's massive fiscal deficit.
